inScope: A dependency-light core package defining Relay wire types and the versioned opaque cursor format
A servant package providing the `RelayPage` combinator with server, client, link, and OpenAPI 3.1 support via openapi-hs/servant-openapi-hs
A hasql package implementing the keyset-pagination engine (predicate generation, ORDER BY/LIMIT n+1, hasNextPage/hasPreviousPage derivation, backward-page row reversal)
A conformance package that consuming services can run against their own endpoints to prove no-skip/no-duplicate pagination behavior
Guides for human developers and coding agents on declaring endpoints, base queries, and sort specifications
Support for declarative, typed sort specifications (ordered sort columns plus a unique tie-breaker column) driving cursor and query generation
A cursor fingerprint mechanism guarding against cross-endpoint cursor reuse
Adherence to the Haskell language and API conventions recorded in `docs/adr/1-haskell-language-and-api-conventions.md`, sourced from the `shinzui/haskell-jitsurei` corpus
outOfScope: Migrating `mls-service-v2` or any other existing service to use this library (it is used only as design/failure-mode input)
Cursor encryption or HMAC signing (cursors remain opaque and versioned but not tamper-proof, beyond the cross-endpoint fingerprint check)
summary: This initiative builds `relay-pagination`, a family of Haskell packages that let services built on servant and hasql expose cursor-based pagination APIs conforming to the Relay Cursor Connections Specification over plain REST/JSON (not GraphQL): the four Relay arguments (`first`, `after`, `last`, `before`) become query parameters and the `Connection` (edges with node/cursor, plus pageInfo) becomes the JSON response body. A developer adds a paginated endpoint by declaring it with a `RelayPage` servant combinator and a `Connection MyPayload` result type, writing a base hasql query with no ordering/limit/cursor logic, and declaring a sort specification (ordered sort columns ending in a unique tie-breaker, each with a typed codec); the library then handles argument parsing/validation, opaque cursor decoding, keyset predicate and ORDER BY/LIMIT n+1 generation, query execution, Connection assembly, and OpenAPI 3.1 documentation. The design is driven directly by concrete failure modes observed in the private `mls-service-v2` reference implementation (used only as design input, not migrated) — lossy text/float cursor round-tripping that causes boundary skips, incorrect hasNextPage at exact page boundaries, backward-pagination edge-order violations, ~150 lines of per-table copy-paste, and a non-spec request surface — each of which the new library fixes by construction with exact-precision cursors, a single hasNextPage/hasPreviousPage derivation point, correct edge reversal semantics, one declarative sort-spec-driven engine, and canonical Relay argument names.
userVisibleBehaviors: A developer declares a paginated endpoint using a `RelayPage` servant combinator and a `Connection MyPayload` result type without writing any pagination SQL by hand
Endpoints accept the standard Relay query parameters `first`, `after`, `last`, and `before` instead of ad hoc parameters like `direction`/`cursor`/`count`

Endpoints return a spec-correct Relay `Connection` JSON envelope: `edges` (each with `node` and an opaque `cursor`) plus a `pageInfo` object with `hasNextPage`, `hasPreviousPage`, `startCursor`, and `endCursor`
Malformed or invalid cursors are rejected with an HTTP 400 at the servant layer instead of causing a SQL runtime error

Pagination never skips or duplicates rows at a page boundary, even when many rows share the same sort-key value, because cursors carry exact integer microsecond timestamps compared as proper SQL parameter types

`hasNextPage`/`hasPreviousPage` are always correct, including at the exact boundary where remaining rows equal the requested page size, because they are derived from a single n+1 probe-row computation
Paging backward (`last`/`before`) returns edges in the same canonical order as forward paging, with correct PageInfo semantics for both directions

A developer defines pagination behavior for a new table by declaring one ordered sort specification (columns plus a unique tie-breaker, each with a typed codec) instead of copy-pasting per-table pagination modules
OpenAPI 3.1 documentation for the Relay arguments and Connection response is generated automatically for every paginated endpoint
Cursors are opaque and versioned and carry a fingerprint that prevents reusing a cursor from one endpoint on a different endpoint
A consuming service can run a conformance test suite against its own paginated endpoints to prove no-skip/no-duplicate pagination behavior
Guides are available for both human developers and coding agents describing how to add a Relay-paginated endpoint
